tokens: nominalized verb (forms the subject with の)
predicate (nominal adjective/形状詞 used as predicate)

items.jp: 母がさらを洗っている

translation.pt-BR: Minha mãe está lavando os pratos.
translation.en: My mother is washing the dishes.

items.label: subject
items.explanation: が marks who performs the action; here it presents 母 (mother) as the subject who is washing.

items.jp: あねは うたを うたうのが じょうずです

translation.pt-BR: Minha irmã mais velha canta muito bem.
translation.en: My older sister sings really well.

items.label: subject marker of the ability
items.explanation: が marks うたうの ('singing') as the thing one is good at. It is the particle required by the pattern 〜のがじょうずです.

items.jp: パパは今日仕事が休みだ

translation.pt-BR: Hoje o papai está de folga no trabalho.
translation.en: Today Dad has the day off work.

items.label: subject marker
items.explanation: が marks 仕事 as the specific subject of 休みだ ('work is off'), presenting the new information within the comment about daddy.

items.jp: 新しい仕事が見つかるといいです

translation.pt-BR: Tomara que você ache um trabalho novo.
translation.en: I hope you find a new job.

items.label: marks the subject
items.explanation: が points to 新しい仕事 as what appears/is found; with intransitive verbs like 見つかる, が is used to mark who carries out the action on its own.

items.jp: ご質問がございますか

translation.pt-BR: Tem alguma pergunta?
translation.en: Do you have any questions?

items.label: subject marker
items.explanation: が marks 質問 as that whose existence is being asked about; with existence verbs like ございます/ある one uses が, not を.

items.jp: せんせいは えいごを はなすのが じょうずです

translation.pt-BR: O professor fala inglês muito bem.
translation.en: The teacher speaks English really well.

items.label: subject marker (focus of the ability)
items.explanation: が marks はなすの ('speaking') as the thing the teacher is じょうず at, in the pattern 〜のがじょうずです.

items.jp: 母は料理を作るのがすきです

translation.pt-BR: Minha mãe gosta de cozinhar.
translation.en: My mother likes cooking.

items.label: subject marker (of the liking)
items.explanation: が marks the nominalized action as that which one likes. With すき, the target of liking takes が.

items.jp: 弟は体が弱いです

translation.pt-BR: Meu irmão mais novo tem saúde frágil.
translation.en: My younger brother is in frail health.

items.label: subject marker
items.explanation: が marks 体 (body) as that which is 'weak', in the は…が pattern that links the topic (person) to the described aspect.

items.jp: あの男の人は髭が長い

translation.pt-BR: Aquele homem tem a barba comprida.
translation.en: That man has a long beard.

items.label: subject marker
items.explanation: が marks 髭 as the specific subject described by 長い, within the larger topic.
tokens: part of the head of the topic

items.jp: お金が足りないから少し足す

translation.pt-BR: Como o dinheiro não dá, coloco mais um pouco.
translation.en: Since there isn't enough money, I'll chip in a little more.

items.label: subject
items.explanation: が marks the money as the subject of 足りない, presenting it as new information/focus.

items.jp: 空が青くてきれいだ

translation.pt-BR: O céu está azul e bonito.
translation.en: The sky is blue and beautiful.

items.label: subject marker
items.explanation: が points to 空 (sky) as the subject that possesses the qualities described.

items.jp: わたしが住んでいる町はしずかです

translation.pt-BR: A cidade onde eu moro é tranquila.
translation.en: The city where I live is peaceful.

items.label: subject marker (within the relative clause)
items.explanation: が marks 「わたし」as the subject that performs the action 住んでいる within the clause that modifies 町; in relative clauses it is common to use が (or の) for the internal subject.

items.jp: 春になると花が開く

translation.pt-BR: Quando chega a primavera, as flores desabrocham.
translation.en: When spring comes, the flowers bloom.

items.label: subject marker
items.explanation: が marks 花 as the subject that performs the action of 開く; it presents new information, not an already-known topic.

items.jp: 友だちが作ったケーキはおいしかった

translation.pt-BR: O bolo que minha amiga fez estava delicioso.
translation.en: The cake my friend made was delicious.

items.label: subject marker (within the relative clause)
items.explanation: が marks 「友だち」as the subject of the action 作った within the clause that modifies 「ケーキ」: 'the friend made (the cake)'. This is が marking the subject of a relative clause.

items.jp: わたしは朝はやく起きるのがすきです

translation.pt-BR: Eu gosto de acordar cedo de manhã.
translation.en: I like waking up early in the morning.

items.label: subject marker (of the liking)
items.explanation: が marks the nominalized action as that which one likes. With すき, the target of liking takes が.

items.jp: ７日から学校が始まる

translation.pt-BR: A escola começa a partir do dia 7.
translation.en: School starts from the 7th.

items.label: subject marker
items.explanation: が marks 学校 as the subject performing the event of 始まる; intransitive verbs of occurrence tend to use が to present what happens.
tokens: counter suffix (forms 七日 = なのか, 'the 7th')

items.jp: かれは サッカーを するのが じょうずです

translation.pt-BR: Ele joga futebol muito bem.
translation.en: He plays soccer really well.

items.label: subject marker (focus of the ability)
items.explanation: が points to するの ('playing') as the thing he is じょうず at; in the pattern 〜のがじょうずです, it is が (not を) that marks this action.

items.jp: わたしは えを かくのが へたです

translation.pt-BR: Eu sou ruim em desenhar.
translation.en: I'm bad at drawing.

items.label: subject marker of the ability
items.explanation: が marks かくの as the thing one is bad at. It is the mandatory particle of the pattern 〜のがへたです.

items.jp: この本を読んだことがない

translation.pt-BR: Nunca li este livro.
translation.en: I've never read this book.

items.label: subject marker
items.explanation: が marks こと ("the experience") as the subject of ない; it is what "does not exist" in the construction 〜たことがない.

items.jp: この店には特別なメニューがある

translation.pt-BR: Nesta loja tem um cardápio especial.
translation.en: This store has a special menu.

items.label: marks the subject that exists
items.explanation: が points to the thing whose existence the verb ある affirms; it is the menu that exists (メニューがある).

items.jp: じゃあ、私が行くよ

translation.pt-BR: Então eu vou.
translation.en: Well then, I'll go.

items.label: subject marker
items.explanation: が marks 私 (I) as the subject, emphasizing that it is the speaker who goes ('I am the one who goes').

items.jp: わたしは うたを うたうのが へたです

translation.pt-BR: Eu canto mal.
translation.en: I'm bad at singing.

items.label: subject marker of the predicate
items.explanation: が points to the thing one is bad at: 'singing' is what the person does poorly. The pattern 〜のがへたです.

items.jp: わたしは青い車がほしい

translation.pt-BR: Eu quero um carro azul.
translation.en: I want a blue car.

items.label: marker of the desired object
items.explanation: In the pattern 〜がほしい, what one wants takes が (not を). That is why 車 receives が.

items.jp: 犬は雨の日がきらいです

translation.pt-BR: Cachorro não gosta de dia de chuva.
translation.en: Dogs don't like rainy days.

items.label: marker of the object of the emotion
items.explanation: With きらい the hated object takes が; here が marks the whole group 雨の日 as the target of the dislike.
tokens: object of the emotion (head of 雨の日)

items.jp: アジアには国がたくさんある

translation.pt-BR: Na Ásia tem muitos países.
translation.en: There are many countries in Asia.

items.label: subject marker
items.explanation: が marks 国 ('countries') as the subject that exists, the obligatory pattern with the verb ある.

items.jp: 急げ、電車が来るぞ

translation.pt-BR: Corre, o trem tá chegando!
translation.en: Run, the train's coming!

items.label: subject particle (が)
items.explanation: Marks 電車 as the subject performing the action 来る. が (and not は) is used because it is new/immediate information, a warning of what is happening right now.

items.jp: 台所のガスのにおいがする

translation.pt-BR: Tem cheiro de gás na cozinha.
translation.en: There's a smell of gas in the kitchen.

items.label: marks the subject
items.explanation: が marks におい ('smell') as that which is sensed; in 〜がする the perceived sensation always takes が.

items.jp: 食堂はいつも人がいっぱいだ

translation.pt-BR: O refeitório está sempre cheio de gente.
translation.en: The cafeteria is always full of people.

items.label: subject marker
items.explanation: が marks 人 as the subject of the state "being crowded"; it describes what there is at the place within the topic already set by は.

items.jp: バス代が足りない

translation.pt-BR: O dinheiro da passagem de ônibus não dá.
translation.en: The bus fare money isn't enough.

items.label: subject marker
items.explanation: が marks バス代 as the subject of the verb 足りない; with existence/sufficiency verbs like 足りる, what is lacking normally takes が.

items.jp: やっと電車が来た

translation.pt-BR: Finalmente o trem chegou.
translation.en: The train finally arrived.

items.label: subject marker
items.explanation: が marks 電車 (the train) as the subject that arrived; with verbs of appearance/arrival like 来る, が highlights what appeared on the scene.

items.jp: 先生が話す日本語は分かりやすい

translation.pt-BR: O japonês que o professor fala é fácil de entender.
translation.en: The Japanese the teacher speaks is easy to understand.

items.label: subject marker (within the relative clause)
items.explanation: が marks 「先生」as the subject of 話す within the clause that modifies 「日本語」: 'the teacher speaks (the Japanese)'. This is が marking the subject of a relative clause.

items.jp: 犬が門の近くにいます

translation.pt-BR: Tem um cachorro perto do portão.
translation.en: There's a dog near the gate.

items.label: subject marker
items.explanation: が presents 犬 as the new subject of existence; in 'there is/exists' sentences with いる/ある, が is used, not は.

items.jp: 父は料理をするのが下手です

translation.pt-BR: Meu pai cozinha mal.
translation.en: My father is bad at cooking.

items.label: marks the subject of the evaluation
items.explanation: が marks 'the cooking' as that which 下手 evaluates. Abilities (上手/下手) use が for what is being judged.

items.jp: 明日は都合が悪いです

translation.pt-BR: Amanhã não vai dar pra mim.
translation.en: Tomorrow won't work for me.

items.label: subject marker
items.explanation: が marks 都合 as what is 悪い (bad). In state constructions like 都合が悪い, the が points to what is in a given condition.

items.jp: わたしは月曜日がきらいです

translation.pt-BR: Eu não gosto de segunda-feira.
translation.en: I don't like Mondays.

items.label: marker of the object of the emotion
items.explanation: With きらい the hated object takes が; here が marks 月曜日 as the target of the dislike.
tokens: object of the emotion (the thing that is hated)

items.jp: この町は工業がさかんだ

translation.pt-BR: Nesta cidade a indústria é forte.
translation.en: Industry is strong in this city.

items.label: subject marker
items.explanation: が points to 工業 as the specific subject that has the described characteristic (being prosperous), within the topic 'this town'.

items.jp: 犬が大きな声で吠え出した

translation.pt-BR: O cachorro começou a latir bem alto.
translation.en: The dog started barking really loudly.

items.label: subject marker
items.explanation: が marks 犬 ('dog') as the subject that performs the action of barking.

items.jp: ともだちは えを かくのが じょうずです

translation.pt-BR: Meu amigo desenha muito bem.
translation.en: My friend draws really well.

items.label: subject marker (focus of the ability)
items.explanation: が marks かくの ('drawing') as the thing the friend is じょうず at, following the pattern 〜のがじょうずです.

items.jp: 行きたいです、尤も時間がありませんが

translation.pt-BR: Eu quero ir, embora eu não tenha tempo.
translation.en: I want to go, even though I don't have time.

items.label: subject marker
items.explanation: が marks 時間 as that whose existence is asserted/denied. With existence verbs like ある, what exists (or not) is marked by が.

items.jp: １日から新しい仕事が始まる

translation.pt-BR: O trabalho novo começa no dia 1.
translation.en: The new job starts on the 1st.

items.label: marks the subject
items.explanation: が points to 'the new job' as that which begins; it combines with the intransitive verb 始まる, which takes its subject in が.
tokens: time noun (part of the date: the 1st)

items.jp: 風でドアが開きました

translation.pt-BR: A porta abriu com o vento.
translation.en: The door opened with the wind.

items.label: subject marker
items.explanation: が marks ドア (door) as the subject that undergoes the change; the intransitive verb 開く takes が, not を.

items.jp: バスがなかなか来ない

translation.pt-BR: O ônibus custa a chegar.
translation.en: The bus is slow to arrive.

items.label: marks the subject
items.explanation: が points to バス as the subject that (does not) perform the action. Here it presents an observed fact/situation, hence が and not は.
tokens: adverb (part of なかなか〜ない)

items.jp: 母が料理をする間、私は本を読んでいた

translation.pt-BR: Enquanto minha mãe cozinhava, eu estava lendo um livro.
translation.en: While my mother was cooking, I was reading a book.

items.label: subject of the subordinate clause
items.explanation: が marks 母 as the subject of the action within the 間 ("while THE MOTHER cooks"); within clauses with 間 the subject takes が, not は.

items.jp: 電車がすっとホームに止まった

translation.pt-BR: O trem parou suavemente na plataforma.
translation.en: The train pulled smoothly to a stop at the platform.

items.label: subject marker
items.explanation: が marks 電車 as the subject that performs the action of stopping; with intransitive verbs like 止まる, が is used to point out what undergoes/performs the motion.

items.jp: 私が説明いたします

translation.pt-BR: Eu é que vou explicar.
translation.en: I'm the one who will explain.

items.label: subject particle (with emphasis)
items.explanation: が marks 私 as the subject and, in this context, emphasizes who performs the action ("it's me, and not someone else, who is going to explain").

items.jp: 県下の学校が試合に出ました

translation.pt-BR: Uma escola do estado participou da partida.
translation.en: A school from the state took part in the match.

items.label: marks the subject
items.explanation: が presents 学校 as the subject that performs the action (to participate). が, and not は, is used because it introduces new information, without highlighting it as a topic.

items.jp: 家の後ろに小さい林がある

translation.pt-BR: Atrás de casa tem um bosque pequeno.
translation.en: There's a small grove behind the house.

items.label: subject marker
items.explanation: が marks 林 as the thing whose existence is asserted; with ある/いる what exists takes が, presenting new information.

items.jp: 駅の近くに食堂がある

translation.pt-BR: Perto da estação tem um restaurante simples.
translation.en: There's a cafeteria near the station.

items.label: subject marker
items.explanation: が marks 食堂 as what exists; with ある, what exists comes marked by が.

items.jp: わたしは日本語が少し話せます

translation.pt-BR: Eu falo um pouco de japonês.
translation.en: I speak a little Japanese.

items.label: marks the object of the ability
items.explanation: With the potential form 話せます, what one is able to do is usually marked by が (not を). So 日本語が is 'Japanese' as the target of 'being able to speak'.

items.jp: 子どもがなかなか起きない

translation.pt-BR: A criança custa a acordar.
translation.en: The child is hard to wake up.

items.label: subject marker
items.explanation: が marks 子ども as the subject that does not perform the action of waking up; here it presents the child as new information/focus of the situation described.

items.jp: 空が真っ青できれいです

translation.pt-BR: O céu está azul vivo e lindo.
translation.en: The sky is a vivid, beautiful blue.

items.label: subject marker
items.explanation: が marks 空 (the sky) as the subject that is vivid blue and beautiful.

items.jp: 漢字よりひらがなのほうがやさしい

translation.pt-BR: Hiragana é mais fácil que kanji.
translation.en: Hiragana is easier than kanji.

items.label: marks the subject
items.explanation: が points to ひらがなのほう as what is easier, completing the comparative のほうが.

items.jp: 今日は風が弱いです

translation.pt-BR: Hoje o vento está fraco.
translation.en: The wind is light today.

items.label: subject marker
items.explanation: が marks 風 (wind) as the subject that is weak, in the は…が pattern.

items.jp: あには りょうりを つくるのが へたです

translation.pt-BR: Meu irmão mais velho cozinha mal.
translation.en: My older brother is bad at cooking.

items.label: subject marker of the predicate
items.explanation: が points to the thing one is bad at: 'cooking'. The pattern 〜のがへたです.

items.jp: 弟は野菜がきらいです

translation.pt-BR: Meu irmão mais novo não gosta de verdura.
translation.en: My younger brother doesn't like vegetables.

items.label: marker of the object of the emotion
items.explanation: With きらい the hated object takes が; here が marks 野菜 as the target of the dislike.
tokens: object of the emotion (the thing that is hated)

items.jp: このアパートはペットがだめです

translation.pt-BR: Neste apartamento não pode ter bichinhos de estimação.
translation.en: You can't have pets in this apartment.

items.label: subject marker
items.explanation: が marks ペット as the specific subject of what is だめ (not allowed) within the topic.

items.jp: 母が作れない料理はない

translation.pt-BR: Não existe prato que minha mãe não consiga fazer.
translation.en: There's no dish my mother can't make.

items.label: subject marker
items.explanation: が marks 母 as the subject of the relative clause 母が作れない; in clauses that modify nouns the subject takes が, not は.

items.jp: あの町は掏摸が多い

translation.pt-BR: Naquela cidade tem muito batedor de carteira.
translation.en: There are a lot of pickpockets in that city.

items.label: subject marker
items.explanation: が marks 掏摸 as the subject of 多い; the combination 〜が多い is the standard way to say that something 'exists in large quantity'.

items.jp: むずかしいことばがあります たとえばこの漢字

translation.pt-BR: Tem palavras difíceis, por exemplo este kanji.
translation.en: There are difficult words, for example this kanji.

items.label: marks the subject that exists
items.explanation: が marks ことば ('word') as the subject of the existence verb あります: it is 'what' exists. In existence sentences, が is used, not は.

items.jp: わたしは本を読むのがすきです

translation.pt-BR: Eu gosto de ler livros.
translation.en: I like reading books.

items.label: subject marker (of the liking)
items.explanation: が marks the nominalized action (本を読むの) as that which one likes. With すき, the target of liking takes が, not を.

items.jp: ドアが開く

translation.pt-BR: A porta abre.
translation.en: The door opens.

items.label: marks the subject
items.explanation: が indicates who/what performs the action on its own: ドアが = 'the door'. With intransitive verbs like 開く, what moves/changes is marked by が, not を.

items.jp: ここから海が見られます

translation.pt-BR: Daqui dá para ver o mar.
translation.en: You can see the sea from here.

items.label: subject/object particle
items.explanation: が marks 海 as what can be seen; with potential verbs the object usually takes が instead of を.

items.jp: 急に都合が悪くなりました

translation.pt-BR: De repente o horário não deu mais pra mim.
translation.en: Suddenly the timing no longer worked for me.

items.label: subject marker
items.explanation: が marks 都合 as what underwent the change in 悪くなる: it was the availability that 'became bad'.

items.jp: 犬とねことどちらがかわいいですか

translation.pt-BR: Qual é mais fofo, o cachorro ou o gato?
translation.en: Which is cuter, the dog or the cat?

items.label: subject marker
items.explanation: が marks どちら as the subject of the comparison; どちらが is the fixed pattern for asking which of the two.

items.jp: いろんな人が研究をします

translation.pt-BR: Muitas pessoas diferentes fazem pesquisa.
translation.en: Many people do research.

items.label: subject marker
items.explanation: が marks いろんな人 (various people) as the subject that performs the action.

items.jp: 私が車の運転をしない

translation.pt-BR: Eu não dirijo.
translation.en: I don’t drive.

items.label: subject marker
items.explanation: が points to 私 (I) as the one who does (not) perform the action; it focuses the subject rather than merely presenting it as a topic.

items.jp: かならず近所の人が出てくる

translation.pt-BR: Os vizinhos sempre aparecem.
translation.en: The neighbors always come out.

items.label: marks the subject
items.explanation: が marks 近所の人 as the subject that performs the action of 出てくる.

items.jp: 私が持ち上げるには重すぎるよ。

translation.pt-BR: É pesado demais para eu levantar.
translation.en: It's too heavy for me to lift.

items.label: subject marker
items.explanation: が marks 私 as the subject of the action 持ち上げる within the subordinate clause (the one who would lift).

items.jp: コーヒーを飲むとトイレが近くなるんだ。

translation.pt-BR: Quando tomo café, fico com vontade de ir ao banheiro logo.
translation.en: Coffee goes right through me.

items.label: subject marker
items.explanation: が marks トイレ as the subject that undergoes the change (近くなる).

items.jp: その本には何が書いてあるの？

translation.pt-BR: O que está escrito nesse livro?
translation.en: What's written in the book?

items.label: subject marker
items.explanation: が marks 何 (what) as the subject that appears written (it is the new information being asked about.)

items.jp: 明後日、転校生が来ることになっている。

translation.pt-BR: Depois de amanhã, está combinado que um aluno transferido vai chegar.
translation.en: It's been arranged that a transfer student will arrive the day after tomorrow.

items.label: subject marker
items.explanation: が marks 転校生 (the transfer student) as the subject who performs the action of coming.
tokens: formal noun that nominalizes the preceding clause
verb of the ことになっている pattern

items.jp: 天気が持つかなあ。

translation.pt-BR: Será que o tempo vai aguentar?
translation.en: I wonder if the weather will hold.

items.label: subject marker
items.explanation: が marks 天気 as a neutral subject, placing the focus on the phenomenon itself ('the weather' as such).

items.jp: あいつが言うことって、分かりづらいよなぁ。

translation.pt-BR: O que aquele cara fala é bem difícil de entender, viu.
translation.en: It's hard to understand what he's saying.

items.label: subject particle (が)
items.explanation: Marks あいつ as the subject of 言う within the relative clause: '(the things) that that guy says'.
tokens: verb of the relative clause that modifies こと
formal noun: 言うこと = 'what (he) says'
verb stem of the compound 分かりづらい
adjectival suffix forming 分かりづらい ('hard to understand')

items.jp: 急に天気が悪くなってきた。

translation.pt-BR: De repente o tempo começou a piorar.
translation.en: All of a sudden the weather started to turn bad.

items.label: marks the subject
items.explanation: が highlights 天気 (the weather) as that which undergoes the change 'to worsen'.

items.jp: 体が弱いので、スポーツができません。

translation.pt-BR: Como tenho saúde frágil, não consigo praticar esportes.
translation.en: Since I'm in delicate health, I can't play sports.

items.label: subject marker
items.explanation: が marks 体 as the subject of 弱い ('the body is weak'). In descriptions of states, the subject usually comes with が.

items.jp: 今月、あのスーパーは水曜日が休みです。

translation.pt-BR: Este mês, aquele supermercado folga às quartas-feiras.

items.explanation: が marks 質問 as that which 'exists/there is'. With the verb of existence ある, what exists is marked by が: 質問がある = 'there are questions'.

items.jp: それとこれとは話が別でしょ。

translation.pt-BR: Uma coisa é uma coisa, outra coisa é outra, não é?
translation.en: That and this are different things, aren't they?

items.label: subject marker
items.explanation: が marks 話 ('the matter') as the subject within the fixed expression 話が別.

items.jp: 来月には子どもが生まれるんだよ。

translation.pt-BR: No mês que vem vai nascer um bebê, sabia?
translation.en: We're going to have a baby next month.

items.label: subject marker
items.explanation: 「が」 marks 「子ども」 as the subject of 生まれる; it is new information, hence が and not は.

items.jp: １人で行かないほうがいいよ。

translation.pt-BR: É melhor não ir sozinho, viu.
translation.en: You should not go alone.

items.label: particle marking the subject of the comparison
items.explanation: が links ほう to いい in the 〜ないほうがいい pattern, indicating which option is the 'better' one.
tokens: auxiliary of negation (part of 〜ないほうがいい)

items.jp: 外出しないほうがいいよ。

translation.pt-BR: É melhor você não sair.
translation.en: You'd better not go out.

items.label: subject marker (within the ほうがいい pattern)
items.explanation: が links ほう to いい in the fixed pattern ほうがいい: literally 'the side (of not going out) is good', that is, 'it's better'.
tokens: verbal noun (head of 外出する)
noun of the ほうがいい pattern ("that option")

items.jp: お金が入るそばから、すぐ使ってしまうんだ。

translation.pt-BR: Assim que o dinheiro entra, eu já gasto tudo.
translation.en: I spend money as soon as I get it.

items.label: subject marker
items.explanation: が marks お金 ('money') as the subject that 'comes in' (入る).
tokens: verb (of the 'as soon as one enters' clause)

items.jp: バスだと時間がかかるよ。

translation.pt-BR: De ônibus leva tempo, hein.
translation.en: The bus will take time.

items.label: subject marker (が case)
items.explanation: が marks 時間 ('time') as the grammatical subject of かかる. In the construction 時間がかかる, it is always time that 'is spent/taken'.

items.jp: そこには俺が行かなくちゃいけないんだ。

translation.pt-BR: Sou eu que tenho que ir lá.
translation.en: I have to go there myself.

items.label: subject marker with emphasis
items.explanation: が marks 俺 ('I') as the subject and highlights it, indicating that it is precisely the speaker who must go.

items.jp: どうして誰も私が作ったものを食べようとしないの？

translation.pt-BR: Por que ninguém quer comer o que eu fiz?
translation.en: Why won't anyone eat what I made?

items.label: subject marker (in the relative clause)
items.explanation: が marks 私 as the one who made the thing, within the relative clause 私が作った.
tokens: verb of the relative clause (modifies もの)
head of the object (modified by the relative clause)
